judged_text: setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning the promise or attaching any rejection handler, so a failed fetch leaves the public group members page silently empty. A user viewing /g/<name>/members when the members request fails (403 after the group was made invisible, 500, network drop) gets an empty member table with no error; the removed afterModel propagated the rejection and aborted the transition, so the failure was visible before this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the route no longer returns the `model.findMembers()` promise from `afterModel` (the `afterModel` hook was removed entirely) and instead calls `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` without `return` or error handling. `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and returns that promise, so if the request rejects (403/500/network), nothing in the route will block/abort the transition or surface the error; the template was also changed to render `{{#each m in members}}`, which depends on the `members` property set only on success. This makes it plausible the members list renders empty/undefined on failure where previously a rejected `afterModel` promise would have been propagated.
